title: NDPipe: Exploiting Near-data Processing for Scalable Inference and Continuous Training in Photo Storage
problem: Photo storage systems face performance bottlenecks when performing machine learning inference and training on image data due to data movement between storage and compute resources. Efficient in-situ processing of images at storage locations is needed to improve throughput and reduce synchronization overhead.
motivation: Near-data processing in photo storage servers can significantly improve the efficiency and scalability of machine learning workloads by reducing data movement and leveraging distributed compute resources.
method: NDPipe distributes commodity GPUs across storage servers and performs inference and training directly on image data near storage. It efficiently partitions deep neural network models across multiple storage servers and exploits data parallelism to achieve high training throughput with low synchronization costs. The system optimizes resource utilization in each storage server to maximize efficiency of the near-data processing engine.
key_novelty: Using distributed commodity GPUs in photo storage servers to perform near-data processing for both inference and training with efficient model partitioning and data parallelism across storage servers.
contributions: NDPipe system architecture distributing commodity GPUs in photo storage servers for near-data processing
Efficient DNN model partitioning strategy across distributed storage servers with low synchronization costs
Optimization techniques for maximizing resource utilization in each storage server
Achieves 1.39× higher inference throughput and 2.64× faster training speed with same energy budget
primary_theme: near-data processing for distributed image inference and training
